(p-6248)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surat al-'Asr (the Declining Day, Chapter 103)

It is Makki, and it is said to be Madani. Its verses number three.

(p-6249)
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[1-3] ﴿By time,﴾ ﴿indeed, mankind is in loss,﴾ ﴿except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.﴾

﴿By time﴾: that is, by the age (al-dahr). Allah, the Exalted, swore by it because it contains wondrous events, both those that remain and those that pass. For this reason it is said of it: "the father of wonders." It is also because it is mentioned along with the blessings within it and their opposites, so it alerts man that he is prepared for both loss and happiness. It is also to honor it and magnify its status, as an indirect way of clearing it of the loss and blame attributed to it, as it has been said:

They blame time, yet there is no fault in it, except for the people who are unworthy of time.

It is also permissible that by "al-'asr" is meant the known time in which the 'Asr prayer is obligatory.

The Imam said: It was the custom of the Arabs to gather at the time of 'Asr, converse, and discuss their affairs, and their talk might include what is unseemly or what harms some of them toward others. So people would imagine that the time itself is blameworthy. Therefore Allah swore by it, to alert you that time in itself is not something to be blamed or reviled, as people have become accustomed to saying: "a cursed time," "an hour of misfortune," "an age of evil," and what resembles these. Rather, it counts for good deeds just as it counts for bad ones, and it is the vessel for Allah's sublime affairs of creation, provision, honoring and humbling, lowering and raising. How then could it be blamed in itself? What is blamed is only the detestable acts that occur within it!

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾: that is, in a state of loss, because he has squandered his capital, which is the light of innate nature (fitrah) and the original guidance, by preferring the worldly life and its transient pleasures, veiling himself with them and with time, and wasting the lasting for the sake of the perishable.

﴿Except for those who have believed﴾: that is, in Allah and in what He has sent down of truth, with a faith that has taken possession of their wills, (p-6250) so that they act only in accordance with their beliefs, as He said: ﴿and done righteous deeds﴾. Al-Qashani said: that is, of virtues and good works; that is, they earned them, and so they gained an increase of perfective light above the light of potential (al-isti'dad) which is their capital.

﴿And advised each other to truth﴾: that is, some of them enjoined upon others what Allah has sent down in His Book of commands, and avoiding what He has forbidden of disobedience. ﴿And advised each other to patience﴾: that is, patience over what Allah tests His servants with, or patience upon the truth, for reaching the truth is easy. As for remaining upon it and being patient with it through steadfastness and striving for its sake, that is what manifests the true reality and essence of faith.

Notes:

First: Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah (Key to the Abode of Happiness): Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: If all people reflected on this surah, it would suffice them. The explanation of that is that the stages are four, and by completing them a person attains the utmost of his perfection:

The first: knowing the truth. The second: acting upon it.

The third: teaching it to one who does not know it well. The fourth: being patient in learning it, acting upon it, and teaching it.

So Allah, the Exalted, mentioned the four stages in this surah. In this surah He, glory be to Him, swore by time that every person is in loss, except those who have believed, namely those who knew the truth and affirmed it; this is one stage. And did righteous deeds, namely those who acted upon the truth they knew; this is another. And advised each other to truth, that is, they enjoined it upon one another through teaching and guidance; this is a third stage. ﴿And advised each other to patience﴾: they were patient upon the truth and enjoined upon one another patience with it and steadfastness. This is a fourth stage.

This is the pinnacle of perfection. Perfection is that a person be perfect in himself and perfecting for others. His perfection lies in correcting his two faculties, the cognitive and the practical. The correction of the cognitive faculty is by faith, and the correction of the practical faculty is by doing righteous deeds. Perfecting others is by teaching them, being patient with them, and enjoining patience upon them in knowledge and action. So this surah, despite its brevity, is among the most comprehensive surahs of the Qur'an for all good in its entirety. Praise be to Allah who made His Book sufficient over anything else, a cure from every disease, and a guide to every good. End of quote.

(p-6251)
Second: Al-Razi said: This surah contains a severe warning. That is because He, the Exalted, judged that all people are in loss, except whoever brings these four things: faith, righteous deeds, mutual advising to the truth, and mutual advising to patience. This shows that salvation is contingent upon the totality of these matters, and that just as it is obligatory for the responsible person to attain what concerns himself, so too are there obligations toward others, among them calling to religion, giving sincere counsel, commanding good and forbidding evil, and wishing for one's brother what one wishes for oneself. Then He repeated "advising each other" so that the first would include calling to Allah and the second would include steadfastness upon it. The first is enjoining good, and the second is forbidding evil. From this is His saying: ﴿And forbid what is wrong and be patient over what has afflicted you﴾ [Luqman: 17]. And 'Umar said: May Allah have mercy on the one who presents me with my faults.

Third: Al-Razi said: The verse indicates that the truth is heavy, and that trials accompany it. For this reason He joined the advising to patience with it.

Fourth: The specification of advising to truth and patience, from among their inclusion in righteous deeds, is to show the complete concern for both of them.

The Imam said: Among those deeds are calling to the truth and enjoining patience, but He intended to single out these two matters for mention, because they are the guardians of every good and the head of every affair. The truth is what is established as a firm reality or a sound law, and it is what is indicated by a conclusive proof or by direct observation and witnessing. So the condition for salvation from loss is that people know the truth, bind themselves to it, let it settle in their hearts, and then encourage one another to it, by each calling his companion to believe in the established realities that the intellect does not dispute and that transmitted evidence does not contradict, and by keeping themselves and others far from illusions and imaginings in which souls find no rest and for which no proof guides. This cannot happen except by employing reason and perfecting observation of the cosmos, until the soul is able to repel what arises in it of false illusions. This is a release of the intellect from every restraint, together with the requirement of precision in examination, not going along with recklessness or being deceived (p-6252) by habit and illusion. Whoever does not hold himself to bringing people to the sound truth after knowing it is among the losers. How much you see in this verse, in clear text that admits no interpretation.

Patience is a strength of the soul to bear hardship in performing good deeds, and to bear the distress of being deprived of pleasure when obtaining it would oppose a truth, or what the sound Law does not permit, about which there is no disagreement. And it is bearing pains when calamities befall, without anxiety and without going beyond the bounds of truth and the Law in repelling them. So the condition for salvation from loss is that you be patient and that you enjoin patience upon others, and that you lead them to perfect their faculties with this noble virtue, which is the mother of all virtues. You cannot lead them to it until you yourself are adorned with it; otherwise you would be among those who say but do not do what they say, and then you would not be among those who do righteous deeds. End of quote.

Fifth: The Imam said: He said ﴿and advised each other﴾ and did not say "and enjoined," in order to make clear that salvation from loss is tied to the eagerness of each member of the community for the truth, and each one's inclination to have his people, and whoever is concerned with the matter of truth, advised about it, so that he would advise his companion to seek it, since he cares to see the truth and accept it. So in this compact expression it is as though He explicitly stated their mutual advising to truth and their acceptance of that advice when it is directed to them.

Sixth: Ibn Kathir said: Al-Tabarani related through the chain of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Ubayd Allah ibn Hisn, who said: Two of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when they met, would not part until one of them recited to the other Surat al-'Asr to its end, and then one of them would greet the other with salam. The Imam said: People have thought that this was for blessing, and that is an error. It was rather so that each of them would remind his companion of what is mentioned in it, especially the advising to truth and advising to patience, so that before they separated, each would obtain from the other a counsel of good, if he had it.

Imam al-Razi, may Allah have mercy on him, explained this surah in a separate commentary the like of which has not been preceded, so whoever wishes to expand upon its secrets should refer to it.
